data.name: Kale
data.gender_notes: Kale is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'kala', meaning 'time', 'darkness', or 'black'. In Hindu mythology, Kali is a goddess of time, destruction, and creation. She is also known as the 'Mother of the Universe'. The name Kale carries the meaning “Black, Dark” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kale usually hope their child will grow to embody black, dark and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the power of time and destruction, as well as the creation and rebirth of the universe. Embraces the cyclical nature of life.
data.etymology: Kale belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Black, Dark.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kale total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kale has origins in Hindu culture and it is believed that it is derived from the Sanskrit word 'kala'. This word holds serious significance in Hinduism; it represents time and darkness, which are essential elements of life and the universe. It is also the name of a revered goddess, Kali, who symbolizes creation, preservation, and destruction in the cosmic cycle. The name therefore holds a rich cultural heritage and has been passed down through generations, reflecting the diverse and complex nature of Hindu mythology and tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu mysticism, Kali is revered as a supreme being who embodies the ultimate power and creativity of the universe. She is often depicted as a dark force, symbolizing destruction and transformation, which is necessary for creation and the continuous cycle of life. The name Kale carries this spiritual significance, reminding us of the interconnectedness of all things and the essential role of both creation and destruction in the grand scheme of the universe. It encourages us to embrace change, face our challenges, and have faith in the power of the divine to guide us through life's most difficult moments.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Kale in Sanskrit means 'dark' or 'time'. It symbolizes the depth and mystery of the universe, reminding us of the importance of introspection and understanding the cycles of time.
